statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of anonymous public home, search, watch, mobile and error states; signed-in, upload, purchase and creator-studio flows excluded.

page.notes: Anonymous en-GB experience; fresh browser profiles trigger the consent interstitial.

checkOutcomes.method: representative search/watch screenshot and DOM walkthrough

checkOutcomes.method: representative search/watch screenshot and DOM walkthrough

checkOutcomes.method: desktop/mobile screenshot plus dialog DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Every fresh home, search, and watch capture was covered by a large consent dialog; on mobile it filled the viewport and pushed all actions below the fold.

checkOutcomes.method: desktop/mobile screenshot plus dialog DOM inspection

checkOutcomes.method: desktop/mobile screenshot plus dialog DOM inspection

checkOutcomes.method: mobile layout metrics and target/container-query probe

checkOutcomes.method: mobile layout metrics and target/container-query probe

checkOutcomes.method: mobile layout metrics and target/container-query probe

checkOutcomes.method: anonymous search→watch walkthrough and invalid-state probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Search and watch probes expose descriptive titles, video result links, Play, Search, and Go to home; page purpose and next action are explicit.

checkOutcomes.method: anonymous search→watch walkthrough and invalid-state probe

checkOutcomes.method: anonymous search→watch walkthrough and invalid-state probe

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse, trace, layout observer, HAR summary
checkOutcomes.evidence: The mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.000089 and Lighthouse CLS was 0.001, both comfortably stable.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse, trace, layout observer, HAR summary

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse, trace, layout observer, HAR summary

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits plus screenshot/DOM inspection

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits plus screenshot/DOM inspection

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits plus screenshot/DOM inspection

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits plus screenshot/DOM inspection

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits plus screenshot/DOM inspection

checkOutcomes.method: metadata probes and raw-HTML discoverability comparison

checkOutcomes.method: metadata probes and raw-HTML discoverability comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: The watch page returned 200 and exposed canonical https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uT7MVcCQ4rw without a noindex signal.

checkOutcomes.method: metadata probes and raw-HTML discoverability comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: The watch page exposed two JSON-LD blocks and complete Open Graph video title, description, image dimensions, URL, and embed metadata matching visible content.

checkOutcomes.method: headers, cookies, HAR, trackers, secrets and consent inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: HAR attributed 108 of 144 requests to third-party origins; tracker scan found 9 third-party origins (87 font requests alone), while the consent copy states audience measurement occurs before optional personalization.

checkOutcomes.method: headers, cookies, HAR, trackers, secrets and consent inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No geolocation, notification, camera, or microphone prompt appeared on load; authentication is delegated to accounts.google.com rather than an inline password form.

checkOutcomes.method: headers, cookies, HAR, trackers, secrets and consent inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: HSTS, SAMEORIGIN, nosniff, Permissions-Policy and Trusted Types are present, but Referrer-Policy is missing and CSP retains unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval allowances.

checkOutcomes.method: discoverability, service-worker/manifest and invalid-route probes

checkOutcomes.method: discoverability, service-worker/manifest and invalid-route probes

checkOutcomes.evidence: The initial consent/home load transferred 4.06MB, including 3.04MB JavaScript, despite showing little primary media content.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR resource/third-party budget and Lighthouse waste diagnostics
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent/home HAR recorded 144 requests and 4.06MB before the user chose a consent option, including 98 fetch/XHR requests.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The HAR recorded 108 third-party requests and tracker inventory found 9 third-party origins; fonts.gstatic.com alone received 87 requests.

checkOutcomes.method: discoverability and Lighthouse agentic-browsing audits
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse agentic-browsing score was 0.33, failed accessibility-tree and llms.txt checks, while no WebMCP/agent tool declaration was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: discoverability and Lighthouse agentic-browsing audits
checkOutcomes.evidence: On-device language-model inference is not necessary to the core anonymous browse, search, and watch journeys.

checkOutcomes.method: baseline/post heap summaries and runtime DOM/heap probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten programmatic guide toggles, heap node count fell 1,406,303→1,405,700 and self size rose only 70,902,183→71,024,288 bytes (~0.17%), with HTMLElement count 1046→1045.

checkOutcomes.method: baseline/post heap summaries and runtime DOM/heap probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: A loaded anonymous home/consent state used ~65.5MB JS heap and a 71.0MB heap snapshot; substantial but proportionate to a complex media SPA and stable across the repeated interaction.

checkOutcomes.method: baseline/post heap summaries and runtime DOM/heap probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The live DOM probe found zero disconnected queried elements, and post-interaction HTMLElement/closure/object counts did not grow.

paths.description: Anonymous homepage and consent entry state; represents global shell, navigation, privacy prompt, network and performance.
Anonymous homepage at narrow mobile viewport; represents responsive reflow and touch constraints.
Search results for “web development”; represents listing/filter template and the first half of the primary browse journey.
Public watch page for a known video; represents media, metadata, chapters, recommendations and the primary destination.
Invalid video URL; represents content-not-found and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The consent and anonymous entry experience ignore the system dark-mode preference.
findings.evidence: Default and dark-emulated screenshots retain the same white dialog and light app; computed color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map consent/app surface tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving contrast.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference is not reflected and baseline contrast defects remain.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast screenshot is visually unchanged; Lighthouse fails color contrast and links distinguished only by color.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast treatments and system-color fallbacks, then rerun contrast audits.

findings.summary: A full consent interstitial obscures every audited archetype on a fresh anonymous visit.
findings.evidence: Home, search, and watch screenshots are dominated by the same modal; on 360x800 its decision buttons are below the initial viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-first consent treatment where legally possible; keep essential reject/accept controls visible without scrolling and avoid repeating after a recorded choice.

findings.summary: The anonymous search-to-watch journey is gated by an oversized consent decision before content can be used.
findings.evidence: Direct search and watch URLs render useful content behind a blocking modal in every fresh browser profile.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve a minimal anonymous browse/watch path while consent is undecided and persist the decision reliably.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is well outside the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 8.5s, FCP 6.5s, Speed Index 13.4s and score 0.51; trace LCP is 4.18s.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP critical path, remove redirects, prioritize only the LCP resource, and defer non-critical app/player work.

findings.summary: Large main-thread tasks delay responsiveness.
findings.evidence: Trace records four long tasks, longest 268.78ms and TBT 275.52ms; Lighthouse attributes 2.1s to main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks into yieldable work, schedule by priority, and avoid initializing player/cast/offline modules before needed.

findings.summary: The entry state ships a 4MB, script-heavy dependency graph before consent.
findings.evidence: HAR records 144 requests/4.06MB, 3.04MB script, parser-blocking legacy polyfills/scripts and multiple redirects; largest JS is 2.11MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential modules until consent/interaction, collapse redirects, modernize delivery, and shorten parser-blocking chains.

findings.summary: Large amounts of downloaded JS and CSS are unused on the audited state.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 643KiB unused JavaScript and 156KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by surface and capability; load player, cast, offline, and route-specific CSS only where exercised.

findings.summary: Some controls expose mismatched or missing accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails label-content-name-mismatch and select-name, contributing to accessibility score 0.85.
findings.suggestedFix: Align accessible names with visible labels and associate every select/input with a programmatic label.

findings.summary: Text/link contrast does not consistently meet accessible minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse directly fails color-contrast and link-in-text-block audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise foreground/background contrast and add non-color link affordances such as underlines.

findings.summary: The viewport policy restricts user scaling.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails meta-viewport because user-scalable=no or a maximum scale below 5 is applied in the audited load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and restrictive maximum-scale values; verify 200–400% zoom and reflow.

findings.summary: Several prominent controls expose only 24×24 CSS-pixel hit areas.
findings.evidence: Computed target probe measures Guide and Settings at 24×24, below the commonly usable 44×44 target area.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the icon 24px if desired but enlarge the interactive box and spacing to at least 44×44 CSS px.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during a normal load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console audit fails.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or intentionally handle the recorded runtime/network errors and keep production console output clean.

findings.summary: Production platform hygiene has BFCache, source-map, and DevTools Issues failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports invalid/missing source maps, inspector issues, and one BFCache blocker.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore valid source maps, resolve DevTools Issues, and remove the BFCache blocking lifecycle behavior.

findings.summary: Useful browse and watch content is largely absent for non-JavaScript crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measures 6% raw/rendered word overlap on home and 5% on watch and classifies both as JS shells.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful titles, descriptions, channel/video links, transcript/chapters and recovery content into crawlable HTML.

findings.summary: Strong baseline headers are weakened by CSP allowances and a missing Referrer-Policy.
findings.evidence: Header audit finds CSP unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval and no Referrer-Policy, despite HSTS, Trusted Types, nosniff and frame protection.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval/legacy allowlist policy paths where possible and set an explicit privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy.

findings.summary: The pre-decision page makes a very large third-party request footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR counts 108/144 third-party requests; trackers inventory finds 9 origins and 87 requests to fonts.gstatic.com before consent choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Self-host/cache stable assets, batch essential telemetry, and delay non-essential third-party traffic until purpose and consent justify it.

findings.summary: Core content depends on JavaScript despite large server responses.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML is 875KB–1.34MB yet shares only 5–6% of rendered content words; crawler screenshots omit useful route content.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a meaningful resilient baseline for home/search/watch and hydrate enhancements on top.

findings.summary: The anonymous consent state consumes an excessive network and third-party budget.
findings.evidence: Before primary interaction, HAR transfers 4.06MB over 144 requests, including 3.04MB JS, 98 fetch/XHR requests and 108 third-party requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Define route budgets; defer player/cast/offline modules and background fetches, reduce fonts, and enforce budget regressions in CI.

findings.summary: The experience offers weak machine/agent access to its useful content and actions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic-browsing score is 0.33 with accessibility-tree and llms.txt failures; non-JS content coverage is 5–6%.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose structured, permission-conscious agent capabilities and server-rendered machine-readable content/actions; fix the accessibility tree first.
